question: Can I label an entire section as experimental, but mark one specific endpoint in it as outdated? What are all the lifecycle labels I can use?
ground_truth: You can set the `availability` property at the section level in your `docs.yml` configuration to mark entire sections of your API Reference. For example, setting a section's availability to `beta` automatically marks all endpoints in that section as beta. However, you can override this section-level setting for specific endpoints by setting availability explicitly on individual endpoints - so your deprecated endpoint can be marked as `deprecated` even if the section is marked as `beta`. The available maturity levels include: `stable`, `generally-available`, `in-development`, `pre-release`, `deprecated`, and `beta`, giving you granular control over communicating API maturity. This section-level approach with individual overrides is efficient - you mark the whole section once while maintaining flexibility for exceptions.

metadata.cited_context: You can set the availability for the entire API reference or for specific sections in your `docs.yml` configuration. Options are: `stable`, `generally-available`, `in-development`, `pre-release`, `deprecated`, or `beta`. When you set the availability of a section, all of the endpoints in that section are automatically marked with that availability unless explicitly set otherwise.
